headline: I don't just use AI. I build teams of it.

principles.title: Constitutions, not prompts
principles.text: Every project has an AGENTS.md that fixes canonical physics, keeps originals read-only, puts work in dated session folders, and logs every deviation.

principles.title: Humans hold the gates
principles.text: Agents propose; I accept. Anatomy, activity maps and scientific conclusions each pass an explicit human QC gate.

principles.title: Right model for the job
principles.text: Claude Code and Codex for engineering, Gemini and Antigravity for coordination, local Llama and Gemma for private, cheap tasks.

principles.title: Evidence over vibes
principles.text: Hashes, provenance, failure logs and quantitative reports. A pretty image is never the result.

roadmap: Surrogate PET simulator trained on Monte Carlo output (NASGM-style)
Heterogeneous PET synthesis from uniform activity maps (PAD-style)
Small generative models for PET/CT simulation and dosimetry

learning.text: 45-day medical-imaging AI apprenticeship with a local Gemma tutor and Codex review.

kage-game.watch: Follow one task: it is queued on the ./crew board, built in its own git worktree by Claude Code or Codex, reviewed by a different agent, and merged to main only after I approve.

veritomix-office.watch: Follow one request: Atlas splits it across the department heads, each works with a local specialist, and the results come back through Atlas and my approval gate before anything ships.

animus.watch: Follow the highlighted listing: the router sorts each opportunity into a lane, Claude or Codex opens the link to check it is real, and only verified items reach the board. Dead or duplicate links drop into the archive.
